text:
anya: quick heads-up — bringing up hf model (hf/vec-lite-v2) on Redwood for embedding + reranker evals. baseline HF embeddings and Redwood embeddings are drifting a lot on same prompt set.

mike: sorry to jump in — any obvious tokenization differences? cls/special token mapping? truncation? padding?

anya: i've been comparing tokenizer configs. hf config.json has "truncation_strategy": "longest_first" and a cls_token defined. our conversion tool seems to drop cls into special_tokens_map but then our embed pipeline uses index 0 pooling. suspicious.

jeff: can you paste the config snippet and a tiny repro call?

anya: sure — config.json excerpt:```json
{"pad_token_id":0,"cls_token":"<cls>","truncation_strategy":"longest_first","model_type":"bert-like"}```
call i used in HF:```py
outputs = tokenizer(texts, truncation=True, padding=True, return_tensors='pt')
embs = model(**outputs).pooler_output  # hf pooler uses CLS
```
and in Redwood we do:```py
ids = tokenizer.encode_batch(texts)
pool = embeddings[id==0]  # take first token embedding as CLS
```

sophie: aha — two likely issues: 1) HF sometimes inserts special tokens (like CLS) at position 0 explicitly; other tokenizers rely on model embedding of special token id. If converter dropped explicit special token insertion, positions shift. 2) truncation_strategy semantics differ when paired with truncation=True vs calling tokenizer.encode with max_length — that can change which tokens get removed (left vs right).

mike: also check token offsets: HuggingFace fast tokenizers can return offsets and special_tokens_mask. If converter switched to a slow tokenizer, offsets change and so does pooling index.

anya: ran a quick diff: HF token ids for sample A: [101, 523, 99, 102] vs converted Redwood ids: [523, 99, 102] — CLS (101) got removed. cosine sim between HF-cls-emb and Redwood first-token-emb is 0.64, vs hf-cls vs hf-first-token Emb sim 0.95. huge.

jeff: ok that explains magnitude. Two remediation paths: 1) ensure converter preserves explicit special token insertion (i.e., ensure tokenizer.add_special_tokens + tokenizer.model_input_names order), 2) change Redwood pooling to use special token id -> find index where token_id == cls_token_id rather than assume index 0.

anya: i'm in favor of (2) as defensive; we have multiple models with differing special token positions. implement a generic pooling helper:```py
def find_pool_idx(input_ids, cls_id):
    for i,t in enumerate(input_ids):
        if t==cls_id:
            return i
    return 0  # fallback
```

mike: +1. Also add a conversion test that asserts tokenizer.converted.special_tokens_map has cls and pad mapped and that truncation_strategy preserved. Add small unit: run 100 samples and compare token sequences with HF python tokenizer.

sophie: another gotcha — quantized model evals showed slightly different embeddings but the major drift goes away after fixing cls alignment. still seeing a small mean shift (~0.02 cosine) — probably quantization/noise.

emb-bot: auto-eval: after cls-fix, retrieval MRR on dev set improved from 0.42 -> 0.62; cosine distribution mean diff dropped from 0.18 -> 0.03.

anya: will push a PR for pooling fallback + conversion tests. also adding a small doc in onboarding checklist: 
- verify special_tokens_map (cls, sep, pad) preserved
- compare first 32 token ids vs HF for 50 samples
- assert truncation_strategy equivalence (only_first/only_second vs longest_first)
- run small reranker eval to compare MRR before approving model

jeff: don't forget chat templates: some HF chat wrappers insert system message as leading special token; that can offset positions if we later feed to embedder without stripping. add a note.

mike: great. assign to @anya. i'll help with conversion test harness. :thumbsup:

anya: TY. i'll tag you in PR. will rerun quantized evals after fix and post numbers here.

sophie: if anyone hits edgecases, dump token ids + tokens + offsets for a failing sample and paste here. shorter threads help. :smile:
